requested_outcome: Make the result count and sort control compact, clear and readable in every VII discovery world without changing search or sort behavior.
natural_destination: Rendered vacation, spa, event and hourly search result toolbars on mobile and desktop.
authorization_boundary: Local source, tests and local visual verification only. No public deployment is authorized in this turn.

lesson_bundle.reason: The reported defect is primarily a cramped mobile composition problem.
lesson_bundle.acceptance_impact: Verify the first results toolbar at 390px and a narrow mobile width with no horizontal overflow and at most two lines for the count.

lesson_bundle.reason: The request explicitly removes redundant labels and reduces visual weight and spacing.
lesson_bundle.acceptance_impact: The toolbar must use one restrained count, one compact sort trigger and no duplicate sort label.

lesson_bundle.reason: Rendered mobile evidence is needed for a shared search control correction.
lesson_bundle.acceptance_impact: Capture and inspect rendered mobile screenshots rather than accepting source or build evidence alone.

predicted_rejections.rejection: Only the hourly route is fixed while another world still shows the old verbose sort label.
predicted_rejections.prevention: Change the shared sort copy and compact selector treatment, then inspect all four world implementations.
predicted_rejections.acceptance_check: Vacation, spa, event and hourly toolbars all render the recommended option as the localized equivalent of 'Recommended' and hide the redundant compact label.

predicted_rejections.rejection: The result count still breaks into three lines on a phone.
predicted_rejections.prevention: Use shared compact type and flexible layout constraints for every result heading family.
predicted_rejections.acceptance_check: At 390px the result count is one line where space permits and never exceeds two lines at the narrow test width.

predicted_rejections.rejection: The selected menu option remains unreadable on the dark gradient.
predicted_rejections.prevention: Force selected option text and all nested currency/text fragments to inherit a high-contrast white color.
predicted_rejections.acceptance_check: The open selected option has white text and a visible white check indicator on the dark background.

predicted_rejections.rejection: A CSS-only change breaks selector interaction or sort behavior.
predicted_rejections.prevention: Preserve values and callbacks and test opening, choosing another option, closing and retaining the selected value.
predicted_rejections.acceptance_check: The selector opens, exposes the same options, changes sort, closes and keeps its chosen value.

affected_family: Hebrew, English, Russian and French recommended labels

sources.label: User-provided screenshots of the current result count and unreadable selected option
VII cross-world consistency and mobile primary-surface rules

midpoint_gate.trigger: After shared copy and compact selector styling are implemented but before broad visual QA.
checks: Render one mobile hourly result toolbar and inspect count wrapping, sort copy and selected-option contrast

attack_questions: Does any world still display the phrase 'מומלצים מתחלפים' in its result sort control?
Can the result count still wrap to three or more lines at 390px or create horizontal overflow?
Does opening the selector reveal low-contrast selected text or hide the check state?
Did the visual change alter sort state, URLs or result ordering behavior?
adversarial_close.natural_destination_evidence: Local rendered screenshots and interaction traces for representative result routes at mobile and desktop widths.
adversarial_close.affected_family_evidence: Focused tests and a route matrix covering vacation, spa, event and hourly toolbars plus shared component assertions.

effectiveness.baseline: User screenshots show a three-line result count, redundant sort label/copy and unreadable selected text.
effectiveness.target: All four world toolbars pass the same compact-copy, maximum-two-line and selected-contrast checks in one implementation pass.
